Rating: General AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 130,714Chapters: 13/30Kudos: 116

Summary: It has been five months since the events at the reservoir, and life finally seems to have settled into a new norm for Buck and Eddie. Buck is thriving, as he learns to harness the potential in his new abilities, and Eddie as always is right by his side. At home, their bond is flourishing, as they use their down time to truly embrace being a family, while the chaos of work is keeping them on their toes, as the 118 officially embrace their advanced station status. All in all, life is pretty perfect. So what happens when an unwanted phone call, an unexpected opportunity, and an unprecedented storm suddenly upend everything, and set them on a path they never could have imagined. Along with new friends they meet along the way, join Buck and Eddie as they explore the magical world of the elements, and the bonds that tie them to it. - NOTE: It is strongly recommended that you read 'Part 1: Soul of Water' before starting this fic. entry.title: The Silt Behind
entry.summary:
Author: broken_promises

Rating: Teen And Up AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 54,859Chapters: 15/?Kudos: 320

Summary: “What the hell are you doing here?” Eddie asks. It sounds like an accusation. “I, uh— I’m sorry,” Buck stammers, scratching the back of his head sheepishly, his eyes inconspicuously darting down to Eddie’s bloodied hands. “Eddie... What happened?” Eddie’s brows twitch. The anger behind his eyes burns hot and heavy. “No, Buck. We’re not doing this. This is literally the worst time for—” He cuts himself off, aggressively pinching the bridge of his nose. “You don’t get to— to insert yourself like this. Not anymore.” Buck’s heart sinks like a stone in his chest. “You chose this, remember?” Eddie spits, the words dripping with bitter finality. As soon as Eddie says that, Buck’s mouth clicks shut. Because he doesn’t remember choosing any of this. Not the icy silences, nor the irritated glances, nor this suffocating loneliness. All he wished for was to return to his family, not for them to abandon him.   OR: The tsunami is long over. Buck keeps drowning anyway.

The moment his eyes met Hondo’s, he faltered, foot slipping slightly against the rock.“You okay, kid?”It was impressive, the speed with which Buck recollected himself. His past that he has historically been a bit vague about. When a blast from the past appears on a call, he is realizing that he might not have gotten away so scott-free from his past occupation. Cue Eddie noticing. Now, Buck has to navigate the collision between his past and his present.
